messages.subject: Running hidden functions in set_attribute
parts:
Hi.

I have an attribute that depends on global variable. Just before setting the value of that attribute, I need to run a function that updates the global variable.

For example:
set_attribute(keys = "name",
values = function () c(update_global(), update_attribute())

I know that I could bury the global update_global function in the update_attribute one but since I have many places and functions, this may be either unsuitable or inefficient.

Any thoughts will be appreciated. Thank you.

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Running hidden functions in set_attribute
parts:
On Sun, 11 Aug 2019 at 20:03, Wael MOHAMMED <mrwaelm...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi.
>
> I have an attribute that depends on global variable. Just before setting the value of that attribute, I need to run a function that updates the global variable.

So update the global, then the attribute:

set_global("some global", update_global) %>%
set_attribute("some attribute", update_attribute)

where update_attribute calls get_global to retrieve the value you just set.

Iñaki

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Running hidden functions in set_attribute
parts:
Thank you for the quick response.

I am sorry I didn't make myself clear. I am not using a global_attribute, I am using a global variable (defined and updated in the global environment).

On the same note, the reason I am using a global variable is that I have more than 10 of them and I was worried that using global_attributes may slow the simulation. Is that valid? Does the number of attributes affect the speed of the simulation? Is using global environment variables better? Is getting a global environment variables quicker than getting a simulation environment attribute?

Thank you for your kind support.
